items.title: How bad can a $2.97 ADC be?
items.raw_content: For almost all of my embedded work I’ve used the ADCs included with microcontrollers. These are cheap, relatively fast, and not particularly good. While they sport impressive-sounding 12- and 16-bit readouts, the effective number of bits (ENOB) is usually around 8 or 9. Recently I’ve been playing with the ADS1115. It’s a dedicated ADC from TI module which plausibly delivers 16 bit accuracy.
items.title_zh: 2.97 美元的 ADC 能差到什么程度？
items.summary: The author compares the ADCs built into microcontrollers, whose effective number of bits is usually around 8 or 9, with TI's dedicated ADS1115, which he says plausibly delivers 16-bit accuracy.

items.title: SmolBSD – build your own minimal BSD system
items.raw_content: smolBSD helps you create a minimal NetBSD-based virtual machine that boots and starts a service in a couple milliseconds. No prior NetBSD installation is required. Create and start a microvm from any GNU/Linux, NetBSD, or macOS system. PVH boot and various optimizations enable NetBSD/amd64 and NetBSD/i386 to directly boot QEMU or Firecracker in about 10 ms on modern x86 CPUs.
items.title_zh: SmolBSD：构建你自己的极简 BSD 系统
items.summary: SmolBSD creates minimal NetBSD-based virtual machines that boot and start a service in milliseconds, using PVH boot to launch under QEMU or Firecracker in about 10 ms on modern x86 CPUs.

items.title: FSF announces Librephone project
items.raw_content: LibrePhone is a new initiative by the FSF with the goal of bringing full freedom to the mobile computing environment. The vast majority of software users around the world use a mobile phone as their primary computing device. After forty years of advocacy for computing freedom, the FSF will now work to bring the right to study, change, share, and modify the programs users depend on in their daily lives to mobile phones. "Forty years ago, when the FSF was founded, our focus was on providing an operating system people could use on desktop and server computers in freedom. Times have changed, technology has progressed, but our commitment to freedom hasn't," said Zoë Kooyman, executive director of the FSF. "A lot of work has been done in mobile phone freedom over the years that we'll be building on. The FSF is now ready to do what is necessary to bring freedom to cell phone users. Given the co
items.title_zh: FSF 宣布 Librephone 项目
items.summary: The Free Software Foundation announced LibrePhone, an initiative aimed at bringing full software freedom to mobile phones; executive director Zoë Kooyman said the group will build on earlier mobile-freedom work.
